fact_text: The exporter's first products were basic T-shirts of low quality, made on local machines, until imported machines let it make better fabrics and garments.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter's first full-container order came through a Hong Kong-based Chinese buying agent, which gave it a way into large buyers while it had never hosted those buyers at its factory.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter says the United States, its first export market, takes about 40% to 45% of its exports, with Spain, Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and France as other markets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter says it makes garments for mid-tier global brands and retailers, including Zara, Pull and Bear, US Polo Association and Foot Locker.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter works mainly as a contract manufacturer, making garments to the buyer's design, tech pack and label rather than selling its own brand.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said it grew exports by 31% in 2025, and that the Pakistani knitwear and garment sector is about USD 5 billion in size, with the exporter's own exports at about USD 30 to 40 million.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter put Pakistan's knitwear and garment export sector at about USD 5 billion, which it described as a large sector with the exporter holding a modest share.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter grew by first renting half a floor, then the back half and more floors, then buying a factory and building a third factory as orders rose.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter's management said it set a policy of not taking bank loans and growing with interest-free, self-funded capital, which it said builds buyer trust.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter's management said paying suppliers on time and keeping to specified fabric weight (GSM) builds buyer trust, and that its customers of 20 to 25 years still place repeat orders.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: Pakistan's main knit exports are fleece hoodies and joggers, zip jackets, sweatshirts, polo shirts, T-shirts and embellished or printed garments, with fleece priced below Bangladesh.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said Pakistan's orders come mostly in the fall season for fleece, while spring orders for lightweight fabrics go to Bangladesh, which is cheaper for those fabrics.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said buyers send one inquiry to many countries and many factories, and the cheapest supplier wins, so Pakistan's high cost of doing business is a key competitive disadvantage.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said Pakistani brands are often 25 to 100 years old and built on decades of research and design, so Pakistan's garment makers remain mostly contract manufacturers rather than brand owners.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said home textiles such as bedsheets and towels are a major Pakistani export, and that denim is also a popular Pakistani export line.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said it started with only four or five permanent staff, while most workers were piece-rate contract workers, and it later grew to a large permanent workforce.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said buyers specify fabric weight in GSM, such as 200 GSM, and deliberate short-weighting is a breach, so each order's quality parameters must be kept.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said rising inflation pushes up wages, which raises garment costs, so controlling inflation is the way to keep the whole economy and export costs cheaper.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter said government should provide industrial areas with infrastructure, guidance and compliance centres, and limit land trading so that new industry can be set up.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)

fact_text: The exporter cited Chinese villages that each specialise in one product, with infrastructure that cut the cost of doing business, as the model for how Pakistan could build export clusters.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Babar’s Journey: From A Small Home Business to Exporting to Global Clothing Brands | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-29)
